question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be discrete random variables with the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown below.

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=-1$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ |

If $F(x,y)$ is the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y,$ find $F(1,4).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables with the joint probability mass function $f(x,y),$ then the corresponding joint CDF is given by

$$
F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)={\sum }_{{x}_{i}\le x}{\sum }_{{y}_{i}\le y}f({x}_{i},{y}_{i}).
$$

By definition, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(1,4) & =P(X\le 1,Y\le 4).\end{aligned}
$$

We start by highlighting all cells in the table that correspond to $X\le 1,Y\le 4.$

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=-1$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ |

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}F(1,4) & ={\sum }_{x\le 1}{\sum }_{y\le 4}f(x,y) \\  & =f(-1,2)+f(-1,4)+f(1,2)+f(1,4) \\  & =0.3+0.2+0.2+0.1 \\  & =0.8.\end{aligned}
$$
